1.explanation: The top-level index.js file is responsible for exporting all React components from the library. It currently exports ProgressIndicator, InlineLoading, Loading, Slider, etc., but there is no entry for ProgressBar. Without adding “export { default as ProgressBar } from './components/ProgressBar';” (and the corresponding component implementation under components/ProgressBar), the <ProgressBar> component cannot be imported or used by consumers—hence the missing functionality.
1.bug_scenario: The user is building an installer UI that shows percent‐complete status of a long‐running process (with a colored bar and numeric percentage). They import <ProgressBar> from Carbon (“carbon-components-react”) and render it, but nothing appears because Carbon currently does not include or export a ProgressBar component. In the screenshot the UI shows a placeholder bar and a “1%” label, but the actual ProgressBar implementation and export are missing.

2.explanation: All React component exports are gathered in packages/react/src/index.js. That file exports ProgressIndicator (and its skeleton) but does not export a ProgressBar component. Because the installer code does `import { ProgressBar } from 'carbon-components-react';` and there is no such export, the ProgressBar is missing in the library. To fix the bug, index.js must be updated to export the new ProgressBar component (and the corresponding files under components/ProgressBar must exist and be imported here). No other files reference ProgressBar, so index.js is the key place to add the component export.
2.bug_scenario: The installer UI is trying to display a percent‐complete Progress Bar (with a colored fill and numeric label) by importing <ProgressBar> from carbon-components-react. However, Carbon currently has no ProgressBar export (only ProgressIndicator for step‐based flows), so the import fails or renders nothing and the desired bar with the percentage never appears.
